mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for the most recent week (-20.9 to -19.3) after three weeks of decline, indicating renewed footfall momentum. This short-term momentum is expected to persist and push RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks as consumers continue resuming in-person shopping habits.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -20.9 to -19.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 28 days is lower than its mean over the last 28 days despite the single-week uptick, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: December in Sydney marks the pre-Christmas shopping peak, a strong seasonal driver of retail and recreation mobility independent of epidemiological trends. As the decision date (Dec 15) sits within the final shopping fortnight before Christmas, RETAIL_REC is expected to rise over the next four weeks as holiday shopping intensifies then tapers post-Christmas.
candidate_trigger: decision date falls within 10 days of December 25
evidence_refs: fact:Australian summer holiday and Christmas shopping season
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean does not rise relative to the prior 28 days despite the seasonal shopping window, the seasonal hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained persistently suppressed around -28 to -30 for four weeks. If TRANSIT drops further below -30, this would likely reflect tightening restrictions or public caution that would also suppress RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks as fewer people travel to retail precincts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has ranged between -27.4 and -29.7 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -30 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC's subsequent 28-day mean does not decline relative to the prior period, the threshold hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility rebounded sharply from -22.1 to -16.9 while RESIDENTIAL mobility edged down from 8.6 to 8.3, suggesting households are substituting outdoor leisure (parks) for indoor retail activity during warm December weather. The interaction of rising PARKS and falling RESIDENTIAL is expected to suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks as leisure time shifts away from shopping venues.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -22.1 to -16.9 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 8.6 to 8.3
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean rises despite concurrent PARKS increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases, the substitution interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has gradually declined across the four-week window (9.1 to 8.3), indicating people are spending modestly less time at home and more time engaged in out-of-home activities generally. This broad behavioral shift is expected to lift RETAIL_REC over the next week as part of the same underlying mobility trend.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined steadily from 9.1 to 8.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's weekly mean does not rise in the week immediately following continued RESIDENTIAL decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized near -15 for the last two weeks after recovering from -23.0, suggesting no new workplace restrictions have been imposed and a steady-state policy regime is in effect. Under this stable regime, RETAIL_REC is expected to continue its gradual recovery over the next four weeks absent new lockdown announcements.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stabilized at approximately -15 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean declines while WORKPLACES remains stable near -15, the steady-state recovery hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES recovery appears to have plateaued at around -15 after a sharp rise from -23.0, having not advanced further in the last two weeks. If WORKPLACES fails to rise above -10 in coming weeks, this signals a stalled commuting recovery that will cap further RETAIL_REC growth over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -10 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES held near -15.1 for the last two weeks without further improvement
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -10 for two weeks yet RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean still rises, the plateau-cap hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of stabilized WORKPLACES (-15) and TRANSIT (-28) mobility alongside volatile but recovering PARKS (-16.9) suggests a mixed commuting-leisure recovery where both work-related and recreational travel jointly support broader out-of-home activity. This joint stabilization and recovery is expected to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks as multiple mobility channels reinforce each other.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have stabilized while PARKS has rebounded over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS all remain stable or improve yet RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean does not increase, the multi-channel interaction hypothesis is rejected.
